qe: Who proposed the 'Five Kingdom Classification' system?
e: Whittaker divided all living organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia in 1969.

qe: Which kingdom includes all 'Prokaryotic' organisms like Bacteria and Blue-green algae?
e: Monera consists of single-celled organisms that do not have a defined nucleus.

qe: Organisms that can live in extreme salty areas are called:
e: Halophiles are a type of Archaebacteria that thrive in high salt concentrations like the Great Salt Lake.

qe: Which of the following is known as 'Connecting link' between plants and animals?
e: Euglena is autotrophic (like plants) in sunlight and heterotrophic (like animals) in the dark.

qe: What is the cell wall of 'Fungi' made of?
e: Chitin is a tough, nitrogen-containing polysaccharide that provides structural support to fungi.

qe: Which organism is known as the 'Slipper Animalcule'?
e: Paramecium has a slipper-like shape and is covered in tiny hairs called cilia.

qe: The symbiotic association between 'Algae' and 'Fungi' is called:
e: Lichens are excellent indicators of air pollution, especially Sulfur Dioxide ($SO_2$).

qe: To which Phylum do 'Sponges' belong?
e: Porifera means 'pore-bearers'; they have a water canal system for feeding and respiration.

qe: Which animal is known as 'Portuguese Man-of-War'?
e: Physalia is a colony of organisms that looks like a single jellyfish and has a powerful sting.

qe: The 'Flame Cells' are the excretory organs of which group?
e: Flatworms like Planaria and Tapeworms use flame cells for osmoregulation and excretion.

qe: Which of the following is the 'Largest Phylum' of the Animal Kingdom?
e: Arthropods (insects, spiders, crabs) make up over 80% of all known animal species.

qe: Insects breathe through tiny holes on the sides of their body called:
e: Spiracles lead to a network of tubes called the tracheal system.

qe: Which animal has 'Blue Blood' due to the presence of Hemocyanin?
e: Hemocyanin contains copper instead of iron, giving the blood a blue color when oxygenated.

qe: To which phylum does the 'Starfish' belong?
e: Echinoderms have a 'spiny skin' and a unique water vascular system for movement.

qe: What is 'Binomial Nomenclature'?
e: Proposed by Linnaeus, e.g., *Homo sapiens* (Human).

qe: Which organism causes 'Sleeping Sickness'?
e: It is transmitted by the bite of the Tsetse fly.

qe: Which group of plants is known as the 'Snakes of the Plant Kingdom'?
e: Pteridophytes (like Ferns) were the first terrestrial plants to have vascular tissues (Xylem//Phloem).

qe: The 'Naked Seeds' are a characteristic of which group?
e: Gymnosperms produce seeds that are not enclosed within an ovary or fruit.

qe: Which bird is the 'Smallest' in the world?
e: The Bee Hummingbird is roughly 5-6 cm long.

qe: The only 'Poisonous Lizard' in the world is:
e: Heloderma is found in the southwestern US and Mexico.

qe: Which of the following is known as the 'Age of Fishes'?
e: The Devonian period saw a massive diversification of fish species in Earth's oceans.

qe: How many 'Heart Chambers' does a typical Fish have?
e: Fishes have a 2-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle) with single circulation.

qe: Which of the following is a 'True Fish'?
e: Starfish is an echinoderm, Silverfish is an insect, and Jellyfish is a coelenterate. Dogfish is a cartilaginous fish.

qe: What is the study of Fishes called?
e: Ichthyology focuses on the structure, classification, and habits of fish.

qe: Which animal is the 'Connecting Link' between Reptiles and Birds?
e: Archaeopteryx had feathers like birds but teeth and a long bony tail like reptiles.

qe: How many heart chambers do 'Amphibians' (like Frogs) usually have?
e: Amphibians have 2 atria and 1 ventricle, allowing for partial mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Cold-blooded' (Poikilothermic) animal?
e: Reptiles, amphibians, and fish cannot regulate their internal body temperature and depend on the environment.

qe: The 'Jacobson's Organ' in snakes is used for the sense of:
e: Snakes use their flicking tongue to bring scent particles to this organ in the roof of their mouth.

qe: Which reptile has a 'Four-chambered' heart, unlike most other reptiles?
e: Crocodiles are the only reptiles with a completely partitioned 4-chambered heart.

qe: The 'Pneumatic Bones' (hollow, air-filled bones) are a characteristic of:
e: Hollow bones reduce body weight, making flight easier for birds.

qe: Which of the following is the 'Fastest' land animal?
e: The Cheetah can reach speeds of up to 110-120 km//h in short bursts.

qe: Which mammal is 'Egg-laying' (Monotreme)?
e: The Platypus and Echidna are primitive mammals that lay eggs but nurse their young with milk.

qe: The 'Largest' animal living on Earth today is the:
e: The Blue Whale is a mammal and can grow up to 30 meters in length.

qe: Which organ do 'Whales' and 'Dolphins' use for respiration?
e: Whales are mammals; they must come to the surface to breathe air into their lungs through blowholes.

qe: The study of 'Birds' is known as:
e: Ornithology covers the study of bird feathers, migration, and behavior.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Marsupial' (pouched mammal)?
e: Kanoaroos give birth to undeveloped young that finish growing inside a pouch.

qe: What is the scientific name of the 'Peacock', the national bird of India?
e: Pavo cristatus is the biological name for the Indian Peafowl.

qe: Which of the following is the 'Largest' living bird in the world?
e: The Ostrich is the largest bird; it is flightless but can run at speeds up to 70 km//h.

qe: Which mammal is capable of 'Echolocation' to navigate and hunt in the dark?
e: Bats and Cetaceans (Whales//Dolphins) use high-frequency sound waves to 'see' their surroundings.

qe: The 'Duck-billed Platypus' is unique because it is a:
e: It shows a link between reptiles and mammals by laying eggs but feeding its young with milk.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Non-poisonous' snake common in India?
e: Pythons are constrictors; they kill prey by squeezing rather than using venom.

qe: Who is known as the 'Father of Taxonomy'?
e: Linnaeus developed the Binomial Nomenclature system for naming organisms.

qe: Viruses are considered a 'Connecting link' between:
e: Viruses are inert crystals outside a host but replicate like living beings inside a cell.

qe: What is the 'Genetic Material' found in the Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV)?
e: TMV was the first virus to be discovered and contains RNA as its genetic material.

qe: The protein coat that surrounds the nucleic acid of a virus is called:
e: The capsid is made of smaller units called capsomeres.

qe: What are 'Bacteriophages'?
e: Bacteriophages are used in research and therapy to kill harmful bacteria.

qe: Which of the following is 'Smaller' than a virus and consists only of free RNA?
e: Viroids cause diseases in plants (like Potato spindle tuber disease) and lack a protein coat.

qe: Abnormally folded proteins that cause brain diseases like 'Mad Cow Disease' are called:
e: Prions are infectious proteins that do not contain any nucleic acid (DNA//RNA).

qe: Which of the following is a 'Cartilaginous Fish' (no bony skeleton)?
e: Sharks and Rays have skeletons made of cartilage, which is lighter and more flexible than bone.

qe: The 'Sea Horse' (Hippocampus) belongs to which group?
e: Despite its horse-like head, the sea horse is a bony fish that breathes through gills.

qe: Which mammal has the 'Longest' gestation period (pregnancy)?
e: Elephants remain pregnant for about 22 months.

qe: What is 'Toxin' secreted by scorpions called?
e: Scorpion venom primarily attacks the nervous system of the prey.

qe: Which bird can 'Fly Backwards'?
e: The unique wing structure of hummingbirds allows them to hover and fly in all directions.

qe: Which group of animals is characterized by the presence of a 'Hollow Nerve Cord' and a 'Notochord'?
e: Chordates include all vertebrates (humans, birds, fish) and some primitive relatives.

qe: The 'Swim Bladder' (Air bladder) in bony fish is used for:
e: By adjusting the gas in the bladder, fish can stay at a specific depth without swimming constantly.

qe: Which reptile is famous for 'Changing Color' to match its environment?
e: Chameleons use specialized cells called chromatophores to change skin color.

qe: The 'National Aquatic Animal' of India is:
e: The Ganges River Dolphin (Susu) is a freshwater mammal found in the Ganga river.

qe: Which group of animals is characterized by the presence of 'Mammary Glands'?
e: The ability to produce milk for offspring is the defining feature of mammals.

qe: The only 'Flying Mammal' is the:
e: Bats are the only mammals capable of true, sustained flight.

qe: What is 'Hibernation'?
e: Cold-blooded animals and some mammals like bears enter a deep sleep to survive winter cold and food scarcity.

qe: Which of the following is considered a 'Living Fossil'?
e: Limulus has remained virtually unchanged for millions of years, surviving multiple mass extinctions.

qe: How many 'Legs' does a typical Insect have?
e: Class Insecta is characterized by having three pairs of jointed legs and usually two pairs of wings.

qe: Which of the following is NOT an insect?
e: Spiders belong to Class Arachnida and have 8 legs, while insects belong to Class Insecta and have 6 legs.

qe: The 'Exoskeleton' of insects and crustaceans is made of:
e: Chitin is a light but extremely tough polysaccharide that protects the internal organs of arthropods.

qe: Which organism is used in 'Sericulture'?
e: Sericulture is the commercial rearing of silkworms for the production of silk.

qe: The 'Pearl' is produced by which animal?
e: When a foreign particle enters the shell, the oyster covers it with layers of nacre to form a pearl.

qe: Which Mollusk is known for its high intelligence and 'Ink Sac' for defense?
e: The Octopus is a cephalopod known for its complex nervous system and ability to camouflage.

qe: The 'Radula' is a rasping organ (tongue-like) found in which group?
e: Mollusks use the radula to scrape or cut food before swallowing.

qe: Which animal is the 'Connecting Link' between Annelids and Arthropods?
e: Peripatus shows segmentations like worms but has jointed legs like insects.

qe: What is 'Ecdysis' (Molting) in insects?
o: Shedding of the old exoskeleton to allow growth
e: Since the chitin shell doesn't grow, the insect must shed it periodically to get bigger.

qe: The 'Social Insects' like Bees and Ants communicate using chemicals called:
e: Pheromones are used to signal danger, food locations, or reproductive readiness.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Social' insect?
e: Termites live in highly organized colonies with a king, queen, soldiers, and workers.

qe: The 'Compound Eye' of an insect is made of thousands of small units called:
e: Ommatidia allow insects to detect fast motion, though their vision is often 'mosaic' or pixelated.

qe: Which animal has a 'Water Vascular System' for locomotion?
e: Echinoderms use hydraulic pressure in their tube feet to move and catch prey.

qe: The 'Book Lungs' are the respiratory organs of:
e: Arachnids use these specialized, leaf-like structures for gas exchange.

qe: What is 'Bioluminescence'?
o: Production of light by living organisms (e.g., Firefly)
e: Fireflies use the enzyme luciferase to produce light for attracting mates.

qe: Which animal is called the 'Farmer’s Friend'?
e: Earthworms aerate the soil and turn organic waste into rich 'vermicompost'.

qe: The 'Malpighian Tubules' of a Cockroach are used for:
e: These tubules extract uric acid from the blood and dump it into the gut.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Parasitic' worm found in the human intestine?
e: Ascaris lumbricoides is a common intestinal parasite, especially in children.

qe: What is 'Estivation'?
o: Summer sleep (to avoid heat and dryness)
e: Many snails and amphibians go into a dormant state during hot, dry summers.

qe: मधुमेह (शुगर) के रोगियों के लिए कौन सा सेलाइन नहीं दिया जाता क्योंकि इसमें ग्लूकोज होता है?
qh: Which se-line bottle is avoided for Diabetic patients because it contains glucose/dextrose?
e: D5 and D10 contain dextrose (sugar), which can dangerously spike blood sugar levels in diabetics. / D5 और D10 में शुगर होती है, इसलिए शुगर के मरीजों को यह नहीं दिया जाता।

qe: किस विटामिन की कमी से 'रिकेट्स' (बच्चों में हड्डियों का पतला होना) होता है?
qh: Which vitamin deficiency leads to 'Rickets' (bone thinning in children)?
e: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption in bones. / विटामिन D हड्डियों में कैल्शियम के अवशोषण के लिए आवश्यक है।

qe: शराब के सेवन या भोजन उबालने के दौरान कौन सा विटामिन नष्ट हो जाता है?
qh: Which vitamin is destroyed during alcohol consumption or by boiling food?
e: Vitamin C is water-soluble and heat-sensitive; it is easily lost during processing. / विटामिन C गर्मी के प्रति संवेदनशील है और उबालने से नष्ट हो जाता है।

qe: 'आंवला' को सूखने के बाद भी विटामिन C का बेहतरीन स्रोत क्यों माना जाता है?
qh: Why is 'Amla' considered a great source of Vitamin C, even when dried?
o: It retains nutrients well | यह पोषक तत्वों को अच्छी तरह बनाए रखता है
e: Amla is unique as its Vitamin C content is highly stable and resistant to heat. / आंवला का विटामिन C गर्मी के प्रति प्रतिरोधी और स्थिर होता है।

qe: पाठ के अनुसार हमें सब्जियों को बहुत गहरा छीलने से क्यों बचना चाहिए?
qh: Why should we avoid peeling vegetables too deeply, according to the lesson?
o: To prevent loss of Vitamin C | विटामिन C के नुकसान को रोकने के लिए
e: Many vitamins, especially Vitamin C, are concentrated just under the skin of vegetables. / विटामिन C सब्जियों की त्वचा के ठीक नीचे होता है।

qe: किस विटामिन को 'एस्कॉर्बिक एसिड' भी कहा जाता है और यह घाव भरने में मदद करता है?
qh: Which vitamin is also known as 'Ascorbic Acid' and helps in healing wounds?
e: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) is essential for tissue repair and collagen production, aiding in wound healing. / विटामिन C घाव भरने और ऊतकों की मरम्मत के लिए आवश्यक है।

qe: कौन सा विटामिन मांस, दूध या अंडे में नहीं पाया जाता है?
qh: Which vitamin is NOT found in meat, milk, or eggs?
e: Animal-based foods are generally poor sources of Vitamin C, which is found in citrus fruits. / विटामिन C मुख्य रूप से खट्टे फलों में पाया जाता है।

qe: किस विटामिन को 'एस्कॉर्बिक एसिड' भी कहा जाता है और यह खट्टे फलों में पाया जाता है?
qh: Which vitamin is also known as 'Ascorbic Acid' and is found in citrus fruits?
e: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) is essential for skin and immunity but is destroyed by boiling or peeling. / विटामिन C त्वचा और प्रतिरक्षा के लिए आवश्यक है लेकिन उबालने या छीलने से नष्ट हो जाता है।

qe: निम्नलिखित में से कौन विटामिन C का स्रोत 'नहीं' है?
qh: Which of the following is NOT a source of Vitamin C?
e: Vitamin C is generally absent in meat, milk, and eggs. / विटामिन C आमतौर पर मांस, दूध और अंडे में नहीं पाया जाता है।

qe: 'मछली के यकृत के तेल' (Fish Liver Oil) में विशेष रूप से कौन सा विटामिन पाया जाता है?
qh: Which vitamin is found in 'Fish Liver Oil' specifically (as discussed in class)?
e: Liver stores fat-soluble vitamins, especially Vitamin A. Fish meat generally has Vitamin D. / लीवर वसा में घुलनशील विटामिन, विशेष रूप से विटामिन A को संचित करता है।

qe: 'आंवला' को विटामिन C का बहुत स्थिर स्रोत क्यों माना जाता है?
qh: Why is 'Amla' considered a very stable source of Vitamin C?
o: It can be dried and stored for a year without losing all Vitamin C | इसे सुखाकर संचित किया जा सकता है
e: Amla retains its Vitamin C even after drying or processing better than many other fruits. / आंवला सुखाने या संसाधित करने के बाद भी अपने विटामिन C को बेहतर तरीके से बनाए रखता है।

qe: 'गोल्डन राइस' (Golden Rice) में कौन सा विटामिन प्रचुर मात्रा में पाया जाता है?
qh: Which vitamin is found in abundance in 'Golden Rice'?
e: Golden rice is a genetically modified variety of rice to produce beta-carotene (Vitamin A). / गोल्डन राइस को विटामिन A की कमी को दूर करने के लिए विशेष रूप से बनाया गया है।

qe: मछली का कौन सा भाग विटामिन A का एक समृद्ध स्रोत है?
qh: Which part of the fish is a rich source of Vitamin A?
e: Fish liver oil is a highly concentrated source of Vitamin A. / मछली के यकृत का तेल विटामिन A का मुख्य स्रोत है।

qe: चावल को पॉलिश करने से उसकी बाहरी परत से कौन सा विटामिन हट जाता है?
qh: Polishing rice removes which vitamin from its outer layer?
e: Polishing removes the husk and bran, which are rich in Thiamine. / पॉलिश करने से थायमिन युक्त भूसी और चोकर निकल जाता है।

qe: आम और पपीता जैसे पीले फल किस विटामिन के समृद्ध स्रोत हैं?
qh: Yellow fruits like Mango and Papaya are rich sources of which vitamin?
e: Yellow and orange fruits contain beta-carotene, which is converted to Vitamin A. / पीले फलों में बीटा-कैरोटीन होता है जो विटामिन A में बदल जाता है।

qe: शरीर निर्माण और ऊतकों की मरम्मत के लिए कौन सा पोषक तत्व जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which nutrient is responsible for body building and tissue repair?
e: Proteins are the building blocks of life, made of amino acids. / प्रोटीन जीवन के आधार खंड हैं, जो अमीनो एसिड से बने होते हैं।

qe: मानव शरीर में ऊर्जा का प्राथमिक संचयी रूप क्या है, जो 9.3 किलो-कैलोरी ऊर्जा देता है?
qh: What is the primary storage form of energy in the human body, providing 9.3 kcal/g?
e: Fat is the most energy-dense nutrient and provides high energy in emergency/fasting. / वसा सबसे अधिक ऊर्जा सघन पोषक तत्व है।

qe: दूध में मुख्य रूप से कौन सी शर्करा पाई जाती है?
qh: Which sugar is specifically found in milk?
e: Lactose is the primary disaccharide found in dairy products. / डेयरी उत्पादों में पाया जाने वाला प्राथमिक डाइसैकराइड लैक्टोज है।

qe: कौन सा पोषक तत्व 4.2 kcal/g प्रदान करता है और दैनिक गतिविधियों के लिए शरीर की पहली पसंद है?
qh: Which nutrient provides 4.2 kcal/g and is the body's first choice for daily activities?
e: Carbohydrates like glucose are oxidized first for immediate energy. / तत्काल ऊर्जा के लिए सबसे पहले कार्बोहाइड्रेट का उपयोग होता है।

qe: कौन सा पादप-आधारित भोजन प्रोटीन का 'समृद्ध स्रोत' माना जाता है?
qh: Which plant-based food is considered a 'rich source' of protein?
e: Soybeans contain about 40% protein, making them an excellent source for vegetarians. / सोयाबीन में उच्च मात्रा में प्रोटीन होता है।

qe: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कार्बोहाइड्रेट मानव शरीर द्वारा सबसे आसानी से पचाया जाता है?
qh: Which of the following carbohydrates is most easily digested by the human body?
e: Monosaccharides like glucose are the simplest form of sugar and are absorbed directly into the blood. / ग्लूकोज जैसे मोनोसैकराइड शर्करा के सबसे सरल रूप हैं और सीधे रक्त में अवशोषित हो जाते हैं।

qe: 'टेबल शुगर' (सुक्रोज) में किस प्रकार का कार्बोहाइड्रेट पाया जाता है?
qh: Which type of carbohydrate is found in 'Table Sugar' (Sucrose)?
e: Sucrose is a disaccharide made of glucose and fructose. / सुक्रोज एक डाइसैकराइड है जो ग्लूकोज और फ्रुक्टोज से बना होता है।

qe: 1 ग्राम 'वसा' से कितनी किलो-कैलोरी ऊर्जा प्राप्त होती है?
qh: How many kilo-calories of energy are provided by 1 gram of 'Fat'?
e: Fat is the most energy-dense nutrient, providing about 9.3 kcal per gram. / वसा सबसे अधिक ऊर्जा सघन पोषक तत्व है, जो प्रति ग्राम लगभग 9.3 किलो-कैलोरी प्रदान करता है।

qe: फलों और शहद में पाई जाने वाली सबसे मीठी प्राकृतिक शर्करा कौन सी है?
qh: What is the sweetest natural sugar found in fruits and honey?
e: Fructose is the sweetest among all natural sugars. / फ्रुक्टोज सभी प्राकृतिक शर्कराओं में सबसे मीठा है।

qe: स्वस्थ मानव शरीर में दीर्घकालिक उपयोग के लिए ऊर्जा किस रूप में संचित होती है?
qh: In which form is energy stored in a healthy human body for long-term use?
e: Fat serves as the body's primary long-term energy reserve. / वसा शरीर के प्राथमिक दीर्घकालिक ऊर्जा भंडार के रूप में कार्य करती है।

qe: 'गुड़' (Gud) को रिफाइंड सफेद चीनी से बेहतर क्यों माना जाता है?
qh: Why is 'Brown Sugar' or 'Jaggery' (Gud) considered better than refined white sugar?
o: It is easier for the body to process/breaks down into glucose naturally | प्राकृतिक रूप से पचने में आसान
e: Jaggery is less processed and more easily converted to glucose without high insulin stress. / गुड़ कम रिफाइंड होता है और बिना उच्च इंसुलिन तनाव के आसानी से ग्लूकोज में बदल जाता है।

qe: कार्बोहाइड्रेट का सबसे सरल रूप क्या है जो तत्काल ऊर्जा प्रदान करता है?
qh: What is the simplest form of carbohydrate that provides instant energy?
e: Glucose is a monosaccharide that cells can directly use for energy. / ग्लूकोज एक मोनोसैकराइड है जिसे कोशिकाएं सीधे ऊर्जा के लिए उपयोग कर सकती हैं।

qe: फलों और शहद में पाया जाने वाला सबसे मीठा प्राकृतिक कार्बोहाइड्रेट कौन सा है?
qh: Which carbohydrate is the sweetest natural sugar found in fruits and honey?
e: Fructose is the sweetest among all natural sugars. / फ्रुक्टोज सभी प्राकृतिक शर्कराओं में सबसे मीठा होता है।

qe: भारी व्यायाम या जिम के दौरान, शरीर ऊर्जा के लिए मुख्य रूप से किस पोषक तत्व को जलाता है?
qh: During heavy exercise or Gym, the body primarily burns which nutrient for energy?
e: Carbohydrates are the primary fuel source for intense physical activity. / कार्बोहाइड्रेट तीव्र शारीरिक गतिविधि के लिए प्राथमिक ईंधन स्रोत हैं।

qe: कौन सी शर्करा विशेष रूप से दूध में पाई जाती है जिसे पचाना कुछ वयस्कों के लिए कठिन हो सकता है?
qh: Which sugar is specifically found in milk and can be difficult for some adults to digest?
e: Lactose is the primary sugar in milk, broken down by the enzyme lactase. / लैक्टोज दूध की मुख्य शर्करा है।

qe: सफेद रिफाइंड चीनी की तुलना में 'गुड़' को स्वास्थ्यवर्धक क्यों माना जाता है?
qh: Why is 'Jaggery' (Gud) considered healthier than white refined sugar?
o: It is easier to digest and less refined | यह पचाने में आसान और कम रिफाइंड है
e: Natural jaggery contains some minerals and is processed more slowly by the body. / प्राकृतिक गुड़ में खनिज होते हैं और शरीर इसे धीरे संसाधित करता है।

qe: मानव आहार में 'प्रोटीन' का प्राथमिक उद्देश्य क्या है?
qh: The primary objective of 'Proteins' in the human diet is ____.
o: Body building and repair | शरीर निर्माण और मरम्मत
e: Proteins are the building blocks of the body used for growth and tissue repair. / प्रोटीन शरीर की वृद्धि और ऊतकों की मरम्मत के लिए उपयोग किए जाते हैं।

qe: वे पोषक तत्व जो शरीर को बीमारियों से बचाते हैं, मुख्य रूप से ____ हैं।
qh: Nutrients that protect the body from diseases are primarily ____.
e: Vitamins and minerals provide immunity and protective functions. / विटामिन और खनिज प्रतिरक्षा और सुरक्षात्मक कार्य प्रदान करते हैं।

qe: शारीरिक गतिविधि के दौरान शरीर को तत्काल ऊर्जा कौन प्रदान करता है?
qh: What provides immediate energy to the body during physical activity?
e: Carbohydrates are the main source of fast energy for the body. / कार्बोहाइड्रेट शरीर के लिए ऊर्जा का मुख्य स्रोत हैं।

qe: What is the chemical name of 'Vitamin B12'?
qh: 'विटामिन B12' का रासायनिक नाम क्या है?
e: It contains Cobalt and is essential for red blood cell formation. / इसमें कोबाल्ट होता है और यह लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं के निर्माण के लिए आवश्यक है।

qe: Which vitamin deficiency causes 'Scurvy'?
qh: किस विटामिन की कमी से 'स्कर्वी' (Scurvy) होता है?
e: Lack of Vitamin C leads to bleeding gums and weakness. / विटामिन C की कमी से मसूड़ों से खून आता है और कमजोरी होती है।

qe: Which vitamin helps in blood clotting?
qh: कौन सा विटामिन रक्त का थक्का जमने में मदद करता है?
e: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of proteins needed for blood clotting. / विटामिन K रक्त के थक्के जमने के लिए आवश्यक प्रोटीन के संश्लेषण के लिए जरूरी है।

qe: मानव शरीर का प्राथमिक निर्माण खंड कौन सा पदार्थ है जिसका उपयोग शरीर के निर्माण और मरम्मत के लिए किया जाता है?
qh: Which substance is the primary building block of the human body and is used for its construction and repair?
e: Proteins are essential for the growth and repair of body tissues like muscles, hair, and nails. / प्रोटीन मांसपेशियों, बालों और नाखूनों जैसे शरीर के ऊतकों की वृद्धि और मरम्मत के लिए आवश्यक हैं।

qe: प्रोटीन कितने अलग-अलग प्रकार के अमीनो एसिड से मिलकर बने होते हैं?
qh: Proteins are made up of how many different types of amino acids?
e: A total of 20 amino acids (10 essential and 10 non-essential) combine to form proteins. / कुल 20 अमीनो एसिड (10 आवश्यक और 10 अनावश्यक) मिलकर प्रोटीन बनाते हैं।

qe: पीयूष ग्रंथि से निकलने वाले शरीर की वृद्धि के लिए जिम्मेदार हार्मोन किसके बने होते हैं?
qh: The hormones responsible for body growth, like the one from the pituitary gland, are made of ____.
e: Most hormones, including Somatotropic hormone (STH), are proteinaceous. / सोमेटोट्रॉपिक हार्मोन (STH) सहित अधिकांश हार्मोन प्रोटीन युक्त होते हैं।

qe: What is the scientific name of Vitamin A?
e: Retinol is essential for the formation of rhodopsin in the eyes, which helps in low-light vision.

qe: Which vitamin is also known as 'Sunshine Vitamin'?
e: Vitamin D is synthesized in the skin when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) rays from sunlight.

qe: Deficiency of which vitamin causes 'Pellagra'?
e: Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of Niacin (B3), characterized by the '3 Ds': Dermatitis, Diarrhea, and Dementia.

qe: Which vitamin contains a metal ion (Cobalt)?
e: Vitamin B12 is also known as Cyanocobalamin because it contains the metal Cobalt at its center.

qe: Which of the following vitamins is water-soluble?
e: Vitamins B and C are water-soluble, while A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble (KEDA).

qe: Scientific name of Vitamin C is:
e: Ascorbic acid is vital for collagen synthesis and immune system function.

qe: Ariboflavinosis is caused by the deficiency of which vitamin?
e: Riboflavin (B2) deficiency causes sores on the mouth corners and inflammation of the tongue.

qe: Which vitamin helps in the absorption of Calcium in the intestine?
e: Vitamin D promotes the synthesis of calcium-binding proteins in the intestinal wall.

qe: A deficiency of Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin) leads to which type of Anemia?
e: Vitamin B12 is crucial for RBC maturation; its lack causes Pernicious Anemia.

qe: Fat-soluble vitamins are stored primarily in which tissue?
e: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are stored in the liver and fatty (adipose) tissues.

qe: Deficiency of Vitamin K leads to:
e: Vitamin K is a co-factor for enzymes that activate blood-clotting factors like prothrombin.

qe: Which part of the Human Brain is responsible for 'Memory and Intelligence'?
qh: मानव मस्तिष्क का कौन सा भाग 'स्मृति और बुद्धि' के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
e: Cerebrum is the largest part and controls learning and memory. / प्रमस्तिष्क सबसे बड़ा भाग है और सीखने व स्मृति को नियंत्रित करता है।

qe: Which part of the 'Cinchona' tree yields the drug Quinine?
qh: 'सिनकोना' के पेड़ के किस भाग से कुनैन (Quinine) दवा प्राप्त होती है?
e: Quinine is used in the treatment of Malaria. / कुनैन का उपयोग मलेरिया के उपचार में किया जाता है।

qe: What is the study of 'Fungi' called?
qh: 'कवक' (Fungi) के अध्ययन को क्या कहा जाता है?
e: Mycology deals with the study of fungi and their properties. / माइकोलॉजी कवक और उनके गुणों के अध्ययन से संबंधित है।

qe: Which part of the brain controls body balance and posture?
qh: मस्तिष्क का कौन सा भाग शरीर के संतुलन और मुद्रा को नियंत्रित करता है?
e: Cerebellum is responsible for voluntary movements. / सेरेबेलम स्वैच्छिक गतिविधियों के लिए जिम्मेदार है।

qe: Which organ is affected by Jaundice?
qh: पीलिया (Jaundice) से कौन सा अंग प्रभावित होता है?
e: High levels of bilirubin cause yellowing of skin. / बिलीरुबिन का उच्च स्तर त्वचा के पीलेपन का कारण बनता है।

qe: The 'Curry Leaf' plant belongs to which family? / 'कढ़ी पत्ता' का पौधा किस परिवार से संबंधित है?
e: It belongs to the Rutaceae family, same as citrus fruits. / यह उसी रुटासी परिवार से है जिससे खट्टे फल संबंधित हैं।

qe: Which gland is called the 'Master Gland'? / किस ग्रंथि को 'मास्टर ग्रंथि' कहा जाता है?
e: Pituitary gland controls other endocrine glands. / पीयूष ग्रंथि अन्य अंतःस्रावी ग्रंथियों को नियंत्रित करती है।
